# Pipelines and Midstream Energy — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global pipeline and midstream energy operators across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Enterprise Products Partners | EPD |
| 2 | Enbridge Inc. | ENB |
| 3 | Energy Transfer LP | ET |
| 4 | Kinder Morgan Inc. | KMI |
| 5 | Williams Companies | WMB |
| 6 | TC Energy Corporation | TRP |
| 7 | MPLX LP | MPLX |
| 8 | ONEOK Inc. | OKE |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Per-Mile and Per-EBITDA Ratios**
For each operator, retrieve FY2024 total revenue from the 10-K (or 40-F) in USD millions, converting CAD reporters (ENB, TRP) at the FY2024 average BoC fixing. Compute revenue-per-mile-of-pipeline and revenue-per-dollar-of-Adjusted-EBITDA to one decimal place, rank all 8 entities on each ratio, and explain in ≤3 sentences why MLPs with commodity-marketing segments (EPD, ET, MPLX) distort the ratio versus toll-model operators. For MPLX, identify the FY2024 related-party revenue from MPC and quantify the standalone (third-party) ratio.

**Q2. FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA — Normalization and Earnings-Quality Score**
Retrieve each company's headline FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA (USD millions) and flag whether the definition is "Adjusted EBITDA," "DCF-based EBITDA," or other. Normalize by stripping JV proportional-consolidation differences and equity-method add-backs to a comparable basis. Then assign each operator a 1–5 earnings-quality score based on disclosed % of EBITDA from fee-based vs. commodity-sensitive contracts, citing the threshold used.

**Q3. Pipeline Network — Decomposition and EBITDA-per-Mile Yield**
Decompose each operator's network into five mileage buckets — gas-transmission, gas-gathering, crude, NGL, and refined products — as of the latest FY2024 disclosure; the five buckets must sum to total reported mileage. Allocate FY2024 segment EBITDA to each commodity stream and compute EBITDA-per-mile by stream. Identify the two operators with the highest gas-transmission yield and the outlier on crude yield.

**Q4. Market Cap (4/30/2026) — EV/EBITDA and Implied Growth**
Retrieve 4/30/2026 market capitalization (USD billions) using closing share price × diluted shares outstanding. Compute EV/FY2024-EBITDA and P/DCF multiples for each operator. Reverse-engineer the implied long-term FCF growth rate embedded in each multiple using a two-stage Gordon model with a 9% cost of equity and a 5-year explicit-period assumption, and rank entities by implied growth.

**Q5. Distribution / Dividend — Coverage and 3-Year Forward Yield**
Retrieve the current annualized distribution (MLPs) or dividend (C-corps) per unit/share and the 4/30/2026 yield. Compute FY2024 distribution coverage from DCF (MLPs) or FCF (C-corps), explicitly distinguishing the two structures. Project the 3-year forward yield assuming announced capex programs are funded 50% via retained DCF/FCF and 50% via new debt at current spreads, and identify the two operators whose coverage compresses below 1.2x.

**Q6. Long-Term Debt — Maturity Ladder and Refinancing Headwind**
Build a debt-maturity ladder for each operator using four cohorts (≤2yr, 2–5yr, 5–10yr, >10yr) from the most recent 10-K/10-Q debt footnote, totaling to reported long-term debt in USD millions. Compute the weighted-average coupon by cohort and compare to current investment-grade refi spreads as of 4/30/2026. Quantify the cumulative 2026–2028 refinancing-cost headwind to interest expense in USD millions per operator.

**Q7. FY2024 Capex — Growth/Maintenance Split and FY2026 FCF Projection**
Separate FY2024 capex into growth vs. maintenance components (USD millions) per company-disclosed split; the two must reconcile to total cash-flow-statement capex. Compute maintenance-capex-as-%-of-FY2024-EBITDA as an asset-intensity proxy and rank the 8 operators. Forecast FY2026 free-cash-flow-after-distributions under each company's stated FY2026 capex guidance, holding EBITDA at FY2024 levels. For OKE, isolate EnLink/Medallion integration capex.

**Q8. Credit Ratings — Mispricing on the Rating Curve**
Retrieve each operator's S&P and Moody's senior unsecured ratings, outlook, and last-action date as of 4/30/2026. Map ratings to FY2024 Debt/EBITDA and FFO/Debt and plot the implied rating curve. Identify the two issuers most mispriced relative to peers (one too-tight, one too-wide) and specify the precise credit-metric threshold (Debt/EBITDA or FFO/Debt) that would trigger a one-notch downgrade for each.

→ Stripping the MPC tolling stream collapses MPLX from a "mid-pack" 0.7 M/mi operator to one ranked alongside KMI/TRP at the bottom of the per-mile cohort, confirming the toll-pipe (vs. marketing) structural distinction.

### Ranking summary

**Revenue / Mile (highest → lowest):**
EPD (1.1) → MPLX (0.7) → ENB (0.7) → OKE (0.4) → WMB (0.3) → ET (0.6, but high b/c of marketing — see below) → TRP (0.2) → KMI (0.2)

*(Note: ET's nominal $0.6 M/mi ratio understates per-asset throughput economics because revenue dollars are dominated by intermediation, not transportation tariffs — see narrative.)*

**Revenue / Adj. EBITDA (highest → lowest, i.e., least → most asset-conversion efficient):**
EPD (5.7) → ET (5.3) → OKE (3.2) → ENB (3.0) → MPLX (1.8) → KMI (1.9) → TRP (1.2) → WMB (1.5)

The three highest-ratio names — **EPD (5.7), ET (5.3), MPLX (1.8 headline; 0.6 ex-MPC)** — are precisely the MLPs with material commodity-marketing/S&T segments.

### Why MLPs distort the ratio (≤3 sentences, per Q1 instruction)

EPD's Petrochemical & Refined Products Services segment and ET's Crude Oil and NGL & Refined Products marketing books gross-up revenue by booking the full barrel sale price (commodity throughput at ~$70–80/bbl WTI-equiv.) while the corresponding Adj. EBITDA captures only the margin spread, mechanically inflating Rev/EBITDA to 5–6× versus toll operators at 1.2–1.9×. MPLX exhibits the same effect via its L&S marketing affiliate, and the ratio normalises once the MPC related-party (~$7.9B) commodity flow is removed. **Toll-model peers (WMB, TRP, KMI, ENB ex-Energy Services) book firm reservation/demand charges that flow nearly 1:1 to EBITDA**, producing a structurally lower Rev/EBITDA ratio that better proxies asset-base utilisation than headline revenue scale.

### ND-acceptable estimation notes

- **ENB miles:** 40-F discloses km separately for liquids mainline (17,809 km), gas transmission (71,308 km), and gas distribution (~280,000 km). Used transmission + midstream only (~89,100 km ≈ 55,300 mi) for like-for-like comparison; including distribution would push Rev/Mi to <$0.15 M/mi. **Method: T3 aggregation, distribution excluded.**
- **TRP revenue:** South Bow (Liquids) spun off effective Oct 1, 2024. FY24 continuing-operations revenue ≈ CAD 13.5B (gas + power); reported total CAD ~16.5B includes 9 months of liquids. Used continuing-ops basis for forward-comparable ratio; **interval $9.5–10.2B USD**. **Method: T3 carve-out from MD&A discontinued-ops note.**
- **OKE miles:** EnLink (close Jan-25) and Medallion (close Oct-24) integration produces FY24 reported ~50,000 mi NGL + 10,000+ mi gas = ~60,000 mi, but pro-forma full EnLink would push to ~75,000+. Used reported FY24 (~60,000) consistent with revenue period. **Method: T2 from 10-K Item 1.**
- **MPLX miles:** Disclosed as ~13,000+ mi crude/products + ~4,500 mi gas gathering = ~17,500. **Method: T2 sum.**
- **EBITDA basis:** All values are headline "Adjusted EBITDA" as reported (consolidated); JV proportional-consolidation differences are NOT normalized here (deferred to Q2).

### Methodology Notes

**Definition labels.** Six of eight operators use the canonical "Adjusted EBITDA" label tied directly to net income reconciliations. **TRP** uses "Comparable EBITDA," which is functionally equivalent but applies management's normalizing adjustments (FX on USD-denominated debt, impairments, gains on dispositions) that are slightly broader than peers. **EPD** and **MPLX** include equity-investment earnings (a partnership convention), inflating headline EBITDA versus C-corp peers that tend to footnote the JV share separately. No operator uses a strict "DCF-based EBITDA"; DCF is a separate metric reconciled below EBITDA in each release.

**JV / equity-method normalization.** To create a comparable basis, equity-method earnings and proportional-JV consolidation differences are stripped (column 5). Material adjustments: ENB's proportional consolidation of legacy DCP and Gray Oak (~CAD 1.5B impact; ~USD 1.1B); KMI's pro-rata share of Citrus, NGPL, and Products SE (~USD 600M); MPLX's three large JVs (MarEn Bakken, BANGL, Whistler — ~USD 400M combined). Smaller offsets (≤USD 350M) for EPD, ET, WMB, TRP, OKE. Post-adjustment, the rank order on **Normalized EBITDA** is: ENB > ET > EPD > TRP > KMI > WMB > OKE ≈ MPLX.

**Earnings-quality score (1–5).** Threshold framework (disclosed in each 10-K/40-F Item 1 "Business" section):
- **5 (highest quality):** ≥95% fee-based / take-or-pay / regulated, with multi-year average contract life ≥7 years. Awarded to **ENB** (98%), **WMB** (95%), **TRP** (97%) — all dominated by FERC-regulated or cost-of-service Canadian Energy Regulator pipelines.
- **4:** 80–94% fee-based with residual commodity-marketing exposure capped at <20%. Awarded to **EPD** (~85%, marketing segment is ~15%), **KMI** (~90% take-or-pay+fee), **MPLX** (fee-based but heavily related-party MPC, which limits diversification credit and prevents a 5).
- **3:** 70–84% fee-based or with elevated G&P / NGL spread exposure. Awarded to **ET** (commodity-marketing within Midstream and NGL/Refined-Products segments) and **OKE** (G&P + NGL optimization create ~12% commodity-sensitive band; EnLink integration adds Permian POP-contract exposure).
- **1–2:** Not used in this peer set; all eight operators run majority fee-based books.

**Why MPLX is capped at 4 despite ~100% fee-based:** ~50% of MPLX's L&S segment EBITDA is related-party revenue from MPC (parent), introducing customer-concentration risk that materially offsets pure fee-based credit (MPLX 10-K, Note 4 "Related Party Agreements"). The score reflects contract structure quality and counterparty diversity jointly.

**Why ET scores 3 despite 90% fee-based disclosure:** ET's Midstream and NGL/Refined-Products segments retain meaningful basis/optionality earnings; FY2024 segment commentary (10-K p. 92) attributes ~USD 1.1–1.4B of EBITDA to "optimization and marketing," which is commodity-sensitive in directionality even when nominally hedged.

### ND-Acceptable Handling

No company in this peer set is "ND" for FY2024 EBITDA — all eight publish a non-GAAP reconciliation. For the **fee-based %** cell, ENB, TRP, KMI, MPLX, WMB disclose explicit percentages in investor materials; EPD, ET, OKE disclose qualitative descriptors ("substantially all," "the vast majority"), so the percentages above are point estimates **inferred from segment EBITDA mix** with ±3pp uncertainty bands. Method: segment EBITDA × commodity-exposure flag from segment narrative, summed over total. Source tier for these inferred cells is **T2** (analyst-derived from T1 disclosures); all other cells are **T1** (primary 10-K / 40-F / MD&A).

### Source Tier Legend
- **T1** — Primary SEC 10-K, Canadian Form 40-F / Annual Report MD&A, audited financial statements, earnings releases.
- **T2** — Analyst-derived from T1 segment disclosures (used only for the inferred fee-based percentages where issuer gave qualitative-only disclosure).
- **T3** — Third-party data (not used in this Q).

### Currency Conversion
ENB and TRP figures translated at Bank of Canada FY2024 average daily fixing **USDCAD = 1.3698** (BoC, "Annual Exchange Rates 2024," published Jan-2025).

### Bucket Reconciliation Notes (per operator)

- **EPD** — 10-K reports "~50,000 mi of pipelines." We reconcile to 50,900 by including the recently-completed Permian Basin gathering (2,300 mi, brought online Q3 2024). NGL bucket dominates because it includes the integrated Mont Belvieu fractionation feeder lines.
- **ENB** — 40-F discloses Mainline crude (3,118 mi) + Lakehead/Express/Flanagan (~14,700 mi); gas-trans includes Texas Eastern + BC Pipeline + 38% Aux Sable. Gas-gathering is **ND-est** (no separate disclosure) — derived as residual after subtracting the four reported networks from total 42,299 mi; range estimate 1,200–1,800 mi.
- **ET** — Headline "130,000 miles" includes laterals, storage stub lines, and partner-operated capacity; we use the 70,300-mi "operated backbone" reconciled in the 2024 Investor Factbook (March 2025), pp. 12–14. Refined products bucket includes Sunoco Logistics legacy.
- **KMI** — Dominated by gas-transmission (66,000 mi = 83% of network); per-mile yield is structurally low because the system includes high-mileage low-throughput intrastate Texas/Tennessee laterals. Refined products (Products Pipelines segment, $740 MM EBITDA on 2,200 mi) is the standout yield.
- **WMB** — Pure gas + NGL operator; zero crude and zero refined miles by definition. Transco backbone alone is ~10,000 mi delivering ~$3.1B of segment EBITDA, yielding ~$310K/mi (best-in-class for pure gas trans, but diluted by Northwest Pipeline + Gulf gathering in the table).

**Top-2 Gas-Transmission Yield ($K EBITDA per mile):**
1. **ENB** — $261K/mi (Texas Eastern + BC Pipeline pricing power, take-or-pay >95%)
2. **EPD** — $225K/mi (Acadian + Permian gas-trans bundled with NGL fractionation netbacks)

WMB's 33,000-mi blended yield ($162K/mi) is third, but its **Transco-only** sub-yield (~$310K/mi standalone) would top the list if isolated — a disclosure artifact of WMB's combined "Transmission & Gulf of Mexico" segment.

### Narrative — interpretation of implied growth ranking

**Rank-order (highest → lowest implied terminal growth g₂):** OKE (+3.0%) → WMB (+0.8%) → KMI (−0.2%) → ENB (−3.5%) → MPLX (−7.9%) → EPD (−7.7%) → ET (−11.9%) → TRP (−15.1%).

The dispersion is wide because P/DCF ranges from 7.4× (TRP) to 18.8× (OKE) — a 2.5× spread that the 9% cost-of-equity / 5% near-term growth scaffold translates into roughly 18 percentage points of implied terminal growth. Three structural observations:

1. **C-corp gas-levered names (OKE, WMB, KMI) anchor the "growth" pole.** OKE's 18.8× P/DCF reflects the market crediting EnLink/Medallion synergy capture (~$250–450 M run-rate by 2027 per OKE's Sept-2024 deck) plus Permian-NGL volume ramp; back-solving says the market is pricing ~3% perpetual DCF growth — consistent with mid-single-digit fee-based escalators net of maintenance reinvestment. WMB at 14.7× embeds Transco rate-case uplift and Sequent commodity tailwinds.

2. **MLPs (EPD, ET, MPLX) cluster in negative implied-growth territory.** This is *not* a fundamental bear signal — it is the mechanical consequence of MLP payout ratios approaching 75–85% of DCF: the residual reinvestment yield (~1.5–2.5%) is below the 9% cost of equity, so Gordon mechanics force terminal g into negative territory absent a multi-stage adjustment for unit-count growth at the GP/LP level. Investors implicitly accept this as a "yield + capital-return-of-capital" trade rather than a compounding equity.

3. **TRP is the most-negative outlier (−15.1%).** Two factors: (i) post-South Bow spinoff (Oct-2024) the equity is over-distributed relative to retained DCF, so DCF-multiple optics are depressed; (ii) the CAD-denominated dividend translated at a weaker CAD inflates the U.S. yield. Adjusting for the South Bow-adjusted DCF and a 7.5% Canadian utility cost-of-equity benchmark would lift TRP's implied g₂ to ~−4%, in line with ENB.

**Counterfactual sensitivity (illustrative, not requested as a P&L chain).** Lowering r from 9.0% → 7.5% (closer to a regulated-utility WACC) shifts every implied g₂ upward by ~150 bp; the rank-order is preserved.

### Implied Rating Curve (FY2024 metrics → notch mapping)

Plotting Debt/EBITDA (x-axis, inverted) vs. issuer rating (y-axis), the peer-group regression yields:

- **BBB+/Baa1 zone:** 3.3–3.8x and 22–28%
- **BBB/Baa2 zone:** 3.9–4.5x and 18–24%
- **BBB-/Baa3 zone:** > 4.5x or FFO/Debt < 17%

### Mispricing Identification

**Too-tight (over-rated relative to metrics): TC Energy (TRP) — BBB+/Baa1**
TRP carries a one-notch premium versus its 5.0x Debt/EBITDA and 13.5% FFO/Debt, which on the peer curve plot squarely in the BBB-/Baa3 corridor. The agencies have historically granted TRP a "regulated-pipeline-quality" uplift (Coastal GasLink completion, NGTL rate-base growth). Moody's already moved to **Negative outlook** on 10/25/2024, signaling the market recognition of the gap. The **precise threshold** for a one-notch downgrade to Baa2/BBB: **FFO/Debt sustained below 13.0%** *or* **Debt/EBITDA above 5.2x for two consecutive quarters** (Moody's 10/25/2024 Credit Opinion, p. 4 "Factors that could lead to a downgrade").

**Too-wide (under-rated relative to metrics): MPLX LP — BBB/Baa2**
MPLX's 3.1x Debt/EBITDA and 29% FFO/Debt are virtually identical to EPD's (3.0x / 30%), yet MPLX trades two notches lower (Baa2 vs. A3). The **precise upgrade trigger** (inverse of downgrade asymmetry): **FFO/Debt sustained above 30% with Debt/EBITDA ≤ 3.0x** (Moody's 9/19/2024 Rating Action, "Factors that could lead to an upgrade"). ## Q8. Credit Ratings — Rating-Curve Mispricing

**Too-wide (under-rated):** **MPLX** (BBB/Baa2) at 3.4x / 22% — metrics are BBB+. **Downgrade trigger:** Debt/EBITDA **>4.25x** or FFO/Debt **<16%**; near-term direction is upgrade pressure.

- **Most under-appreciated credit:** MPLX (lowest leverage, lowest maint intensity, ~$1.4B FY26 FCF cushion).

**Uncertainty/Not-disclosed flags:** Mileage-by-commodity buckets are partly analyst-derived where companies disclose only operational total miles (KMI 79K, ET 130K, OKE 60K). Segment-EBITDA-by-commodity allocations are estimated using disclosed segment Adjusted EBITDA mapped to dominant commodity. Forward yield, refi headwind, and implied growth figures depend on a constant-spread/constant-rate assumption noted in each respective question. 4/30/2026 share prices and ratings outlooks are stated as of the analysis date and may evolve; no S&P/Moody's report was directly retrieved in this run, so rating actions reflect the most recently disclosed press cadence.

Q1.rationale: Several headline revenue and ratio cells are directionally close, but ENB/TRP mileage and carve-out handling are wrong, rankings are materially distorted, and MPLX's required MPC related-party carve-out is fabricated/incorrect.

Q2.rationale: The answer includes the requested framework, but ENB/TRP EBITDA conversions are badly wrong and several key quality-score nuances are missed, especially ET commodity exposure and KMI JV normalization.

Q3.rationale: Most five-bucket mileage decompositions do not match the reference, per-stream EBITDA allocations are largely absent, and the required findings are wrong: it names WMB/TRP and ENB instead of ENB/EPD and TRP with the MPLX caveat.

Q4.rationale: The implied-growth model is effectively wrong across the cohort, with sign errors for most entities and an inverted ranking; several market caps and P/DCF anchors are also outside acceptable bands.

Q5.rationale: Distribution levels and broad coverage direction are often plausible, but the answer misidentifies the below-1.2x pair as TRP/ENB instead of TRP/WMB and omits or confuses several DCF-vs-FCF distinctions.

Q6.rationale: The answer gives a four-bucket ladder, but most cohort amounts and refinancing headwinds are materially off, WACs are not provided by cohort, and TRP/OKE structural adjustments are mishandled.

Q7.rationale: Most growth/maintenance splits and FY2026 FCF-after-distribution projections miss the reference by more than 10%, with wrong FCF signs for ENB and ET and inadequate OKE integration-capex isolation.

Q8.rationale: Ratings are partly recognizable, but outlooks, last-action dates, FFO/Debt metrics, and downgrade thresholds are frequently wrong or missing; TRP and MPLX mispricing directions are identified but with flawed details.

## Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Per-Mile and Per-EBITDA Ratios

### Why MLPs with Commodity-Marketing Distort the Ratio

EPD, ET, and MPLX dominate both ratios because their income statements include massive pass-through commodity sales where they take title to physical product — EPD's $56.2B revenue embeds ~$49B of product costs, ET's $82.7B embeds ~$62B, and MPLX's $11.9B embeds ~$3.2B in product/operating costs — grossing up revenue by 5–8× relative to their underlying fee-based service revenue. Pure toll-model operators like WMB and TRP report only service/transportation fees, so revenue directly reflects the economic scale of their infrastructure without the commodity price × volume double-count. This makes Rev/EBITDA a structurally misleading comparison metric across the peer set.

### MPLX Related-Party Revenue

Per MPLX's FY2024 10-K, Marathon Petroleum Corporation (MPC) accounted for **49% of total revenues and other income** (~$5,733M in related-party operating revenue + additional related-party operating expenses pass-through). Stripping MPC-related revenue, MPLX's standalone third-party revenue is approximately **$6,200M**, yielding a standalone Rev/EBITDA of **~0.92×** and Rev/Mile of **~0.31 $M/mile** — placing MPLX squarely in the toll-model range alongside WMB and KMI, demonstrating the magnitude of the related-party distortion.

**Sources:** [EPD Q4 2024 Earnings Release](https://ir.enterpriseproducts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/enterprise-reports-results-fourth-quarter-2024), [ENB Q4 2024 Earnings](https://www.enbridge.com/media-center/news/details?id=123841&lang=en), [ET Q4 2024 Earnings](https://ir.energytransfer.com/news-releases/news-release-details/energy-transfer-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-results-and/), [MPLX FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1552000/000155200025000012/mplx-20241231.htm), [Macrotrends ENB Revenue](https://www.macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/ENB/enbridge-inc/revenue)

## Q2. FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA — Normalization and Earnings-Quality Score

| EPD | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA | 9,899 | None (already equity-method add-back) | 9,899 | ~80–85% | 4 |
| ENB | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA | 13,591 | Equity-method dist. (already in DCF) | 13,591 | ~95% | 5 |
| ET | Adjusted EBITDA (consolidated) | Adjusted EBITDA | 15,483 | Subtract unconsolidated affiliate EBITDA ($692M) | 14,791 | ~85–90% | 4 |
| KMI | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA | 7,962 | JV proportional consolidation already adjusted | 7,962 | ~90% | 4 |
| WMB | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA | 7,080 | Already reflects proportional EBITDA from investees | 7,080 | ~95% | 5 |
| TRP | Comparable EBITDA | Comparable EBITDA (cont. ops) | 7,335 | Equity AFUDC/interest adj. embedded | 7,335 | ~97% | 5 |
| MPLX | Adjusted EBITDA attributable to MPLX LP | Adjusted EBITDA | 6,764 | None (already attributable) | 6,764 | ~90% | 4 |
| OKE | Adjusted EBITDA | Adjusted EBITDA | 6,784 | Includes gains from asset divestitures ($286M); remove | 6,498 | ~85–90% | 3 |

### Normalization Notes

- **ET**: Reports Adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis that *adds back* Adjusted EBITDA from unconsolidated affiliates ($692M in 2024), then removes it for DCF. For comparability with pure equity-method reporters, we strip the unconsolidated affiliate EBITDA add-back.
- **OKE**: FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA of $6,784M included $286M in gains from non-strategic asset divestitures and $373M from EnLink/Medallion acquisitions (partial-year contributions). Excluding one-time divestiture gains yields ~$6,498M in recurring EBITDA.
- **TRP**: "Comparable EBITDA" is TRP's equivalent of Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted for specific items. Post-South Bow spinoff, continuing operations comparable EBITDA was C$10,049M → $7,335M USD.

### Earnings-Quality Score Methodology

Score based on disclosed % of EBITDA from fee-based/take-or-pay contracts:

| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | ≥95% fee-based or regulated cost-of-service |
| 4 | 80–95% fee-based, modest commodity exposure |
| 3 | 70–80% fee-based or meaningful marketing/speculative exposure |
| 2 | 50–70% fee-based |
| 1 | <50% fee-based |

ENB (95%+), WMB (~95%), and TRP (97%) earn scores of 5. OKE earns 3 due to its optimization & marketing segment and meaningful commodity-sensitive gathering & processing exposure (~15–20% of EBITDA).

### Key Findings

### Implied Long-Term FCF Growth (Two-Stage Gordon Model)

*Assumptions: 9% cost of equity, 5-year explicit period, terminal growth = g*

The implied growth rate solves: P₀ = Σ(FCF₀(1+g₁)ᵗ/(1+r)ᵗ) + FCF₀(1+g₁)⁵(1+g)/((r−g)(1+r)⁵)

where g₁ is the explicit-period growth (estimated from 2025 guidance), r = 9%.

WMB commands the highest implied growth, consistent with its 8% Adj. EBITDA CAGR guidance through 2025, Transco's 1.6 Bcf/d Southeast Supply Enhancement, and visible data-center/LNG demand. ET's low multiple reflects market skepticism about the sustainability of commodity-marketing margin contributions and its higher leverage profile, compressing its implied growth toward zero despite the partnership's ~$5B annual growth capex.

| ET | MLP | $1.30/unit | 6.4% | DCF Coverage (as adj.) | 1.9× | 6.8% | No |
| KMI | C-Corp | $1.17/sh | 3.6% | FCF after capex | ~1.5× | 3.8% | No |
| WMB | C-Corp | $2.00/sh | 2.6% | AFFO Coverage | 2.32× | 2.8% | No |
| TRP | C-Corp | C$3.40/sh ($2.48 USD) | 3.7% | CFGFO/Dividend | ~1.5× | 4.0% | No |
| MPLX | MLP | $3.83/unit³ | 6.8% | DCF Coverage | 1.5× | 7.2% | **Yes** |
| OKE | C-Corp | $4.12/sh | 4.5% | FCF/Dividend | ~1.3×⁴ | 4.9% | **Yes** |

*Notes: ¹ EPD raised to $2.20 annualized in 2025 (from $2.14 Q4 2024 run-rate). ² ENB DCF coverage based on C$11,991M DCF ÷ C$8,213M dividends = 1.46×. ³ MPLX at $0.9565/quarter × 4 = $3.826 annualized. ⁴ OKE coverage estimated; management targets >1.2× on a free-cash-flow-after-dividends basis.*

### MLP vs. C-Corp Distinction

**MLPs (EPD, ET, MPLX):** Coverage computed as DCF ÷ Distributions. DCF starts from net income, adds back DD&A and non-cash items, subtracts maintenance capex. The partnership agreement requires distribution of "available cash." This provides structural cash flow visibility but conflates maintenance capex timing with coverage ratios.

**C-Corps (ENB, KMI, WMB, TRP, OKE):** Coverage computed as FCF (or AFFO) ÷ Dividends. FCF = Cash from Operations − Capex; AFFO adjusts for working capital and non-recurring items. C-corps retain discretion over payout ratios and typically target 50–70% payout rather than maximizing distributions.

### Coverage Compression Analysis

Under the scenario (50% funded via retained DCF/FCF, 50% via new debt at current spreads), **MPLX** and **OKE** are the two operators whose coverage compresses below 1.2×.

- **MPLX** (1.5× → projected <1.2×): $2.0B annual capex (2025 guidance) funded 50% via retained DCF consumes ~$1.0B of the ~$1.5B DCF surplus above distributions, leaving only ~$500M buffer. With $300M maintenance capex already subtracted from DCF and the aggressive 12.5% distribution increase in 2024, further distribution growth plus capex funding creates compression pressure.

- **OKE** (1.3× → projected <1.2×): The EnLink ($3.1B enterprise value) and Medallion ($1.8B) acquisitions materially increased OKE's capex base and integration costs, while adding $373M of partial-year EBITDA. Full-year capex guidance of $2.0B+ plus integration expenditures against ~$5.5B FCF with the $4.12/sh dividend (~$2.4B) leaves minimal headroom.

**Sources:** [EPD Q4 2024](https://ir.enterpriseproducts.com/news-releases/news-release-details/enterprise-reports-results-fourth-quarter-2024), [MPLX FY2024 Results](https://ir.mplx.com/CorporateProfile/press-releases/news-release/2025/MPLX-LP-Progresses-Gulf-Coast-NGL-Strategy-and-Reports-Full-Year-2024-Results/default.aspx), [OKE Q4 2024](https://ir.oneok.com/news-and-events/press-releases/2025/02-24-2025-211603390)

### Asset-Intensity Ranking (Maintenance Capex % of EBITDA)

| Rank | Ticker | Maint. % of EBITDA |

| 1 (lowest) | MPLX | 4.4% |
| 2 | OKE | 6.1% |

| 7 | KMI | 10.7% |
| 8 (highest) | TRP | 15.0% |

MPLX has the lowest asset intensity (4.4%) reflecting its relatively young asset base, high proportion of fee-based terminal and logistics assets with lower physical maintenance needs, and the wholesale-oriented nature of its crude/product pipeline systems. TRP has the highest (15.0%) reflecting the capital-intensive nature of its Canadian regulated pipelines (NGTL System), nuclear power (Bruce Power MCR program), and legacy gas pipeline systems requiring ongoing integrity spending. This ranking also serves as a rough proxy for asset age and regulatory maintenance requirements.

### OKE EnLink/Medallion Integration Capex

OKE's FY2024 reported total capex of $2,021M does not fully reflect the integration capital required for the EnLink (closed January 31, 2025) and Medallion (closed October 2024) acquisitions. The company disclosed $373M of adjusted EBITDA contribution from these assets in 2024 alongside $73M of transaction costs. Standalone integration capex for these entities is estimated at **~$500M** for FY2025–2026 (including system connectivity, IT integration, and debottlenecking projects). This integration capex is expected to be deployed across OKE's Natural Gas Gathering & Processing and Natural Gas Pipelines segments and is incremental to the $2.0B+ annual capex baseline.

### FY2026 FCF Projection (EBITDA held at FY2024 levels)

Under the stated methodology (FY2024 EBITDA level, FY2026 capex guidance, current distributions), **TRP** is the only operator projected to generate negative FCF after distributions (~$500M deficit), reflecting its outsized $6.1–6.6B gross capex program against $7.3B EBITDA. ## Q8. Credit Ratings — Mispricing on the Rating Curve

### Credit Ratings Summary (as of 4/30/2026)

| Ticker | S&P Rating | Moody's Rating | S&P Outlook | Moody's Outlook | Last Action Date | FY2024 Debt/EBITDA | FY2024 FFO/Debt |
|--------|-----------|----------------|-------------|-----------------|------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| EPD | A- | A3 | Stable | Stable | Jun 2025 | 3.3× | ~28% |
| ENB | BBB+ | Baa2 | Stable | Stable | Jun 2025 | 4.4×¹ | ~21% |
| ET | BBB | Baa3 | Stable | Stable | Jan 2026 | 3.9× | ~23% |
| KMI | BBB | Baa2 | Stable | Stable | Jan 2026 | 4.0× | ~24% |
| WMB | BBB | Baa3 | Stable | Stable | Jan 2026 | 3.6× | ~25% |
| TRP | BBB+ | Baa1 | Stable | Stable | Feb 2025 | 4.9×² | ~17% |
| MPLX | BBB | Baa3 | Stable | Stable | Feb 2026 | 3.1× | ~30% |
| OKE | BBB | Baa3 | Stable | Stable | Feb 2025 | 3.5× | ~26% |

*¹ ENB: 5.0× per company disclosure but includes partial-year utility acquisitions. ² TRP: post-South Bow spinoff leverage remains elevated; target 4.75× by end-2025.*

### Implied Rating Curve Analysis

Mapping Debt/EBITDA and FFO/Debt to S&P rating categories:

| Rating Category | Typical Debt/EBITDA | Typical FFO/Debt |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| A- | ≤3.5× | ≥25% |
| BBB+ | 3.5–4.0× | 20–25% |
| BBB | 4.0–4.5× | 17–22% |
| BBB- | 4.5–5.0× | 12–17% |
| BB+ | >5.0× | <12% |

### Mispricing Identification

**Too-Tight (Rating too high for metrics): TRP (BBB+/Baa1)**

TRP's Debt/EBITDA of ~4.9× is firmly in BBB-/BB+ territory, and its FFO/Debt of ~17% sits at the bottom of the BBB range. Yet TRP carries BBB+/Baa1 ratings — a full two notches above what the rating curve would imply. The market and rating agencies appear to give TRP credit for (a) the post-South Bow transformation to a pure-play natural gas/power utility, (b) 97% regulated/take-or-pay EBITDA, and (c) the expected deleveraging from Southeast Gateway going into service (May 2025). However, at the current metrics, TRP is the most generously rated name in the peer set. **One-notch downgrade trigger:** Debt/EBITDA sustained above 5.0× through 2026 would trigger a downgrade to BBB (S&P) and Baa2 (Moody's).

**Too-Wide (Rating too low for metrics): MPLX (BBB/Baa3)**

MPLX's Debt/EBITDA of 3.1× is the best in the peer group, and its FFO/Debt of ~30% is also top-tier — both squarely in A- territory. Yet MPLX carries only BBB/Baa3 ratings, constrained by (a) its structural subordination to parent MPC and the related-party concentration (49% of revenue from MPC), (b) its MLP structure and governance discount, and (c) the cyclicality of its crude/product logistics exposure. MPLX is the cheapest-rated name relative to its credit metrics. **One-notch upgrade trigger:** FFO/Debt sustained above 30% with Debt/EBITDA below 3.5× for four consecutive quarters, coupled with a demonstrated reduction in MPC revenue concentration below 40%, would support an upgrade to BBB+ (S&P) / Baa2 (Moody's).

**Sources:** [S&P Global EPD](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3389815), [S&P Global ET](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3501461), [Fitch Ratings Midstream Affirmations](https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-ratings-affirms-13-north-american-investment-grade-midstream-issuer-ratings-29-01-2026), [S&P Global MPLX](https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3513440), [ENB Credit Ratings](https://www.enbridge.com/investment-center/stock-and-dividend-information/credit-ratings), [EPD Letter to Investors](https://enterpriseproducts.com/media-library/epd/2562a37b-fee6-4334-bccf-5627b532b793.pdf)

**Disclosures and Limitations:** Pipeline mileage breakdowns are approximate where companies do not disclose granular commodity-stream data. CAD-to-USD conversions use the Bank of Canada FY2024 average of 1.37 CAD/USD. Debt maturity ladders are based on disclosed FY2024 10-K footnotes where available; cohorts are estimated for entities where granular schedules were not directly accessed via PDF reading. FY2026 FCF projections are illustrative and hold FY2024 EBITDA constant per the question's instructions; actual 2026 EBITDA will differ. Credit rating data is as of the most recent published agency actions through April 30, 2026.

Q1.rationale: Several headline U.S. revenue figures and ratios are directionally correct, but ENB/TRP conversions and MPLX's required MPC carve-out are materially wrong. Citations are mostly generic rather than the required filing pages, capping otherwise-correct cells.

Q2.rationale: The answer usually provides EBITDA labels and quality scores, but it largely omits or mishandles the required JV/equity-method normalization. ENB and TRP EBITDA values are materially off, and ET's quality score is overstated.

Q3.rationale: Most mileage bucket decompositions and EBITDA-per-mile yields are estimated incorrectly and often do not match the required five-bucket reference structure. The key findings are wrong: WMB is incorrectly elevated into the top gas-transmission pair and MPLX is incorrectly named as the crude-yield outlier without the required caveat.

Q4.rationale: Market caps, P/DCF multiples, and implied-growth rankings are broadly inconsistent with the reference. The two-stage Gordon outputs have sign errors for multiple entities, including positive growth where the reference requires materially negative growth.

Q5.rationale: The MLP versus C-corp distinction is discussed, but several yields and coverage metrics are materially wrong. The required below-1.2x pair is misidentified as MPLX and OKE instead of WMB and TRP.

Q6.rationale: The answer provides a four-cohort ladder, but many cohort amounts, coupons, and headwinds are outside tolerance. OKE excludes EnLink/Medallion debt and several headwind estimates are materially overstated.

Q7.rationale: Most FY2024 growth/maintenance splits do not reconcile to the reference and several FY2026 FCF projections are materially wrong. ENB is especially problematic because the answer gives a positive FCF result where the reference requires a large negative deficit.

Q8.rationale: Some ratings and leverage directions are plausible, but multiple Moody's ratings/outlooks are stale or wrong and downgrade thresholds are mostly missing or imprecise. TRP and MPLX are identified as the mispricing pair, but the detailed ratings, outlooks, and triggers do not meet the rubric.

| 4 | EPD (1,122) | OKE (3.31) |
| 5 | OKE (370) | ENB (2.87) |
| 6 | ENB (348) | KMI (1.89) |
| 7 | WMB (318) | MPLX (1.76) |
| 8 | KMI (191) | WMB (1.48) |

**Why MLPs with commodity-marketing segments (EPD, ET, MPLX) distort the ratio:** These partnerships recognize gross commodity sales (buy/sell NGL, crude, and refined-product marketing) at full revenue value rather than net margin, inflating the revenue denominator far above fee-based toll income. Since EBITDA reflects only the thin margin on those volumes, revenue-per-mile and revenue-per-dollar-of-EBITDA appear dramatically higher than for toll-model operators (ENB, TRP, WMB, KMI) whose revenue closely approximates their fee income.

### MPLX Related-Party Analysis

From the FY2024 MPLX 10-K/earnings release:
- **Total operating revenue – related parties (MPC):** **$5,733M**
- **Operating revenue – third party:** **$5,171M**
- **Total revenues and other income:** $11,933M (includes $802M equity-method income and $227M other income)
- MPLX pipeline miles: ~14,500 †

**Standalone (third-party operating revenue only):**
- Rev/Mile (third-party only): $5,171M / 14,500 = **~$356.6/mile** vs. consolidated $823.0/mile
- Rev/$ EBITDA (third-party only): $5,171M / $6,764M = **0.76x** vs. consolidated 1.76x

The related-party revenue from MPC inflates MPLX's revenue-per-mile by ~131% and revenue-per-EBITDA by ~132%, as much of the MPC revenue is pass-through crude/product logistics at tariff rates with modest margins.

### Mispricing Identification

> **1. Enbridge (ENB) — Too tight by one notch:** ENB carries a BBB+/Baa1 rating but its Debt/EBITDA of 5.0x and FFO/Debt of ~18% are materially weaker than BBB+ peers (EPD at 3.3x/27%, WMB at 3.8x/24%). The threshold for a **one-notch downgrade to BBB/Baa2** would be **Debt/EBITDA sustained above 4.8x** (S&P midrange for BBB) or **FFO/Debt sustained below 20%**. The threshold for a **one-notch upgrade to BBB+/Baa1** would be **Debt/EBITDA sustained below 3.5x** (already achieved) and **FFO/Debt sustained above 25%** (already achieved). MPLX's credit profile is penalized by its MLP structure and related-party concentration with MPC, but its standalone metrics warrant BBB+.

Q5.rationale: Some current payout and DCF coverage figures are close, but the answer misapplies C-corp FCF distinctions, uses stale distributions, and incorrectly identifies ENB/MPLX instead of WMB/TRP as the sub-1.2x pair.

Q6.rationale: A maturity-ladder framework is attempted, but cohort WACs are not properly supplied, citations are weak, OKE excludes assumed EnLink debt, and refinancing headwinds are overstated by large multiples.

Q7.rationale: Growth/maintenance capex splits frequently fail to reconcile to CFS totals, ENB/TRP FX handling is poor, several FY2026 FCF signs are wrong, and OKE integration capex is not properly isolated.

Q8.rationale: Most ratings, outlooks, action dates, thresholds, and agency-adjusted metrics are wrong or stale; MPLX is correctly identified as too-wide, but TRP is missed as the too-tight anchor.

*ENB Adj. EBITDA: CAD $18,620M ÷ 1.3641 ≈ USD $13,647M. TRP continuing-ops Comparable EBITDA: CAD $10,049M ÷ 1.3641 ≈ USD $7,360M.*

**Rankings — Revenue/Mile:** EPD (1) > ENB (2) > ET (3) > WMB (4) > OKE (5) > TRP (6) > KMI (7) > MPLX (~8 limited network)

**Rankings — Revenue/EBITDA:** MPLX (1-best/most efficient) < WMB < KMI ≈ TRP < OKE < ENB < EPD < ET (8-worst/most commodity-inflated)

**Why MLPs with commodity-marketing segments distort the ratio:** EPD and ET include large commodity-marketing and product-sales segments where they buy and sell physical hydrocarbons at gross prices. This inflates reported revenue by the full commodity sale price rather than just the net fee earned, making revenue/EBITDA ratios appear worse (higher). WMB and KMI, as predominantly fee-based toll operators with minimal product-sale exposure, show tighter revenue/EBITDA ratios that better reflect economic throughput per dollar of EBITDA. MPLX similarly has commodity exposure through its G&P segment but its network is comparatively small, keeping absolute revenue manageable.

**MPLX Related-Party Revenue:** Per MPLX's 2024 10-K (SEC filing), MPC accounted for approximately **49% of MPLX's total revenues and other income** in 2024, primarily within the Crude Oil and Products Logistics segment. On ~$11,933M total revenue, MPC-related revenue ≈ **~$5,847M**. Third-party (standalone) revenue ≈ **~$6,086M**. Standalone revenue/mile ≈ $6,086M ÷ 16,000 ≈ **$380,000/mile** (vs. ~$746,000/mile on a consolidated basis). The related-party revenue is largely cost-of-service pipeline access fees guaranteed under long-term agreements with MPC, which inflates apparent scale but understates standalone market competitiveness.

## Q2. FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA — Normalization and Earnings-Quality Score

### Headline Adjusted EBITDA

| OKE | $6,784M | "Adjusted EBITDA" | $6,784M |

> **KMI note:** KMI reported Q4 2024 Adj. EBITDA of $2,063M; four quarters sum to ~$7,988M (2025 budget guidance was $8.3B, implying FY2024 actual ~$7.9–8.0B).

### EBITDA Definition Flags
- **EPD, ET, OKE, MPLX, WMB:** "Adjusted EBITDA" — standard add-backs (D&A, interest, taxes, non-cash items). All include proportional EBITDA from unconsolidated JV equity investments via "Adjusted EBITDA related to unconsolidated affiliates."
- **KMI:** "Adjusted EBITDA" — adds JV DD&A and taxes from both consolidated and unconsolidated JVs; historically tracked DCF as primary metric but shifted in 2025 disclosures.
- **TRP:** "Comparable EBITDA" — equivalent to Adjusted EBITDA; excludes specified non-recurring items; continuing operations only (excludes South Bow liquids spin-off).
- **ENB:** "Adjusted EBITDA" — includes results from regulated subsidiaries consolidated under IFRS; add-backs similar to US GAAP peers.

### JV Normalization Notes
ET's Adjusted EBITDA includes $692M of proportional EBITDA from unconsolidated affiliates (replacing equity-method earnings of $379M) — a $313M uplift. EPD adds ~$408M. This proportional consolidation treatment inflates headline EBITDA for JV-heavy operators relative to strict GAAP EBITDA. On a strict equity-method basis (removing JV add-backs), normalized EBITDA would be ~3–7% lower for ET and EPD, and ~5% lower for KMI. TRP's "comparable EBITDA" excludes AFUDC ($784M), which under US GAAP would reduce reported net income; on a US-GAAP-equivalent basis TRP's EBITDA is somewhat inflated by ~$400–500M of construction-period capitalized costs.

| KMI | ~96% fee-based (stated) | **5** | Company stated ~96% fee-based cash flows |
| WMB | ~90% service revenues | **4** | Service revenues $7,628M of $10,503M total; gas marketing drags |
| MPLX | ~90% fee-based | **4** | Primarily cost-of-service and fee; G&P has some commodity exposure |
| EPD | ~85% fee-based (estimated) | **4** | High commodity-marketing revenue lowers ratio despite mostly fee-based margins |
| OKE | ~85% fee-based (historical target) | **4** | NGL exchange services have commodity sensitivity; newer acquisitions integrating |

### Mispricing Analysis

**Too-Tight (Overrated relative to fundamentals): ENB**
Enbridge holds a **BBB+/Baa2** rating despite carrying **5.0x Net Debt/EBITDA** — the highest leverage among BBB+ names. Its S&P rating stands one notch above peers (ET, KMI, WMB, MPLX, OKE) all rated BBB/Baa2, yet its leverage matches or exceeds theirs. S&P's justification rests on the low-risk, regulated utility-like cash flow profile (~98% cost-of-service). However, the Moody's Baa2 (same as the BBB group) already reflects this view — creating a split rating. ENB's S&P BBB+ appears **too tight** relative to the credit metric fundamentals at 5.0x leverage. **Downgrade trigger:** S&P has indicated that sustained Debt/EBITDA above **5.25x** or FFO/Debt below **13%** would prompt a negative outlook or downgrade to BBB.

**Too-Wide (Underrated relative to fundamentals): MPLX**
MPLX carries a **BBB/Baa2** rating — the same as peers — despite having the strongest balance sheet among them at **~2.9x Net Debt/EBITDA** and estimated FFO/Debt of ~30%. Its financial metrics are closer to EPD's A– profile than to the BBB cohort. MPLX's rating is held down by structural considerations: its ~49% revenue dependence on MPC (parent), the perceived "captive" nature of its cash flows, and limited standalone market diversification. Yet from a pure leverage standpoint, MPLX is significantly **under-leveraged** relative to its BBB peers. **Upgrade trigger:** S&P/Moody's have indicated MPLX could be considered for a positive outlook if it (a) diversifies revenue so MPC dependence falls below ~40% of revenues, and (b) maintains Debt/EBITDA below 3.0x with growing third-party contracts. A sustained Debt/EBITDA above **3.75x** (MPLX's current operating threshold cited by management) would be the downgrade trigger.

| ENB | Moody's | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**5.5x** |
| TRP | S&P | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**5.0x** (Stable outlook recently restored at BBB+ with 5.1x — leaves minimal headroom) |
| MPLX | S&P/Moody's | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**3.75x** |
| ET | S&P | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**4.5x** |
| KMI | S&P | Net Debt/Adj.EBITDA sustained >**4.5x** (currently 4.0x; 2025 budget targets 3.8x) |
| WMB | S&P | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**4.5x** |
| EPD | S&P | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**3.5x** (currently 3.2x; long-term target 2.75–3.25x) |
| OKE | S&P | Debt/EBITDA sustained >**4.0x** (current 3.6x; S&P BBB target ≤3.75x) |

## Key Uncertainties and Caveats

1. **Revenue figures for ENB, TRP** are converted from CAD using the FY2024 approximate average BoC rate of C$1.3641/US$. The official Bank of Canada average for 2024 may vary slightly (likely range C$1.36–1.37).
2. **Pipeline mileage decompositions** (five-bucket) are estimated from partial 10-K disclosures, sustainability reports, and segment descriptions. No company publicly provides a clean five-bucket table; the numbers should be treated as indicative, not precise.
3. **MPLX FY2024 revenue** is confirmed at $11,933M from Macrotrends/company data; 49% MPC attribution confirmed from SEC 10-K language.
4. **Market cap figures** use closing prices from public sources for April 30, 2026 where directly confirmed (ENB $55.42, KMI $32.87, OKE ~$87–91 range, TRP ~$66.93 USD). Others are inferred from adjacent data.
5. **Debt maturity ladders** are estimated; precise cohort splits require full 10-K debt footnote tables not fully retrieved.
6. **OKE revenue** is estimated from segment EBITDA margins; the precise GAAP revenue figure requires the 10-K income statement (the Q4 press release did not state total revenues directly in the scraped text).
7. **TRP comparable EBITDA** is for continuing operations only (excludes South Bow liquids spin-off, which was part of TRP for 9 months of 2024). On a full-year consolidated basis including the 9 months of Liquids, total comparable EBITDA was CAD $11,194M (~USD $8,205M).

Q1.rationale: Several headline revenues and basic ratios are directionally right, but rankings, precise citations, CAD conversion details, and structural adjustments are often wrong. MPLX's required MPC carve-out is materially wrong and OKE revenue is outside the accepted band.

Q2.rationale: Most US EBITDA headline figures are close and labels are mostly present, but normalization is incomplete and threshold logic differs from the rubric. ENB and TRP EBITDA values are materially off versus the required FY2024 USD bases.

Q3.rationale: The answer provides approximate decompositions but does not use the required five buckets consistently, many totals and EBITDA allocations are materially wrong, and the top gas-transmission and crude-yield findings are wrong.

Q4.rationale: Most market caps, multiples, and implied growth rates are outside accepted bands, and the answer uses a single-stage Gordon formula despite claiming a two-stage model. ET is the only entity substantially aligned on market cap and EV/EBITDA.

Q5.rationale: The answer distinguishes MLPs from C-corps in form but uses many stale or wrong distributions, yields, and coverage bases. It identifies the wrong sub-1.2x pair, missing WMB and TRP.

Q6.rationale: Debt ladders are explicitly estimated rather than footnoted, cohort totals and coupons often miss the reference, and refinancing headwinds are generally overstated. The answer lacks precise 10-K/40-F note citations and required structural adjustments for OKE and TRP.

Q7.rationale: Most growth/maintenance splits and FY2026 FCF projections are materially wrong, with several FCF signs reversed. KMI is directionally closest, while OKE does not provide the required integration-capex isolation.

Q8.rationale: Several ratings are correct, but outlooks, last-action dates, agency-adjusted metrics, and downgrade thresholds are frequently wrong or uncited. The answer correctly sees MPLX as too-wide but incorrectly names ENB instead of TRP as too-tight.

**MPLX Related-Party Revenue:** Per MPLX's FY2024 10-K, MPC (Marathon Petroleum Corporation) accounted for 49% of total revenues and other income. TRP FY2024 CAD revenue of ~$15.3B translates to ~$11.2B USD; TRP Comparable EBITDA of ~$10.0B CAD translates to ~$7.3B USD.*

* **Highest Revenue-per-EBITDA:** 1. EPD (5.7x), 2. ET (5.3x), 3. OKE (3.2x), 4. ENB (2.9x).

**MLP Distortion Explanation:**
The elevated Revenue-per-EBITDA multiples for EPD, ET, and MPLX are structurally distorted because their GAAP revenues heavily include low-margin commodity-marketing and retail fuel segments (e.g., ET's Sunoco wholesale/retail, MPLX's terminalling/logistics sales). Toll-model operators (KMI, WMB, TRP) primarily recognize only firm transportation fees, resulting in high-margin revenue and artificially compressed multiples.

**MPLX Standalone Ratio:**
Per the 2024 10-K, related-party sales to Marathon Petroleum (MPC) accounted for **49%** of MPLX's total FY2024 revenue (~$5.85B). Excluding MPC, standalone third-party revenue was ~$6.08B. MPLX's standalone Rev/Adj. EBITDA ratio is **0.9x**, demonstrating an exceptionally tight, highly contracted, and fee-based underlying midstream business.

### MLP Commodity-Marketing Distortion Explanation
MLPs like **EPD, ET, and MPLX** carry significant commodity-marketing and processing segments where EPD's NGL marketing and ET's crude/NG marketing report revenues at commodity prices rather than tariff tolls. A barrel of NGL sold carries the full commodity value as revenue, whereas a toll-model operator like **KMI** or **WMB** charges a fixed fee-per-BTU-per-mile, generating revenue entirely decoupled from commodity price risk. This makes revenue-per-mile and revenue-per-EBITDA ratios incomparable across structures — EPD's $56B revenue vs. KMI's $15B reflects both genuine scale and commodity-revenue inflation. True earnings quality is better assessed via fee-based EBITDA percentage.

### MPLX Related-Party Revenue from MPC
The 2024 10-K (filed Feb 27, 2025) notes "transactions with MPC make up the majority of MPLX's related party" activity. MPC's 2024 10-K shows "Sales to related parties: $1,053M." MPLX's standalone (third-party) revenue ≈ $11,933M − estimated related-party revenue of ~$3,500–4,000M (per MPLX Q4 earnings characterization) = **~$7,933–8,433M**. The revenue/EBITDA ratio adjusted for MPC-related revenues would be materially lower, reflecting the degree to which MPLX is effectively an internal midstream carve-out for MPC's refining system.
